images.statement: The Branch Connector Images page in the Zscaler Admin Console provides the ability to download Branch Connector or Branch Connector & App Connector virtual machine images; Branch Connector images include App Connectors that have not yet been provisioned, and deploying Branch Connector & App Connector requires selecting the combined instance and configuring the deployment properties accordingly.

quotes: The Branch Connector Images page in the Zscaler Admin Console provides the ability to download your Branch Connector or Branch Connector & App Connector virtual machine (VM) images.
Branch Connector images include App Connectors that have not yet been provisioned.
To deploy Branch Connector & App Connector, you must select the combined instance and configure the deployment properties accordingly.

image-formats.statement: The VMware page has the administrator download the Branch Connector Open Virtual Appliance (OVA) image file for VMware ESXi, the Hyper-V page the Branch Connector Virtual Hard Disk v2 (VHDX) image, and the Linux KVM page the Branch Connector image, all from the Branch Connector Images page.

quotes: Download the Branch Connector Open Virtual Appliance (OVA) image file for VMware ESXi from the Branch Connector Images page.

iac-templates.statement: Infrastructure as Code (IaC) deployment templates are available in GitHub to assist in deploying Branch Connector or Branch Connector & App Connector in VMware ESXi or Linux KVM, and are not available for Branch Connector deployment on Hyper-V platforms; the VMware ESXi section lists four starter templates: bc, bc_ha (high availability), bc_ac (with App Connector) and bc_ha_ac (with App Connector and high availability).

quotes: Infrastructure as Code (IaC) deployment templates are available in GitHub to assist in the deployment of Zscaler Branch Connector or Branch Connector & App Connector in VMware ESXi or Linux KVM.
IaC deployment templates are not available for Branch Connector deployment on Hyper-V platforms.
Use the Starter Deployment Template (bc) to deploy your Branch Connector.
Use the Starter Deployment Template with High-Availability (bc_ha) to deploy your Branch Connector with high availability.
Use the Starter Deployment Template with App Connector (bc_ac) to deploy your Branch Connector & App Connector.
Use the Starter Deployment Template with App Connector and High-Availability (bc_ha_ac) to deploy your Branch Connector & App Connector with high availability.
Infrastructure as Code (IaC) deployment templates are not available for Branch Connector deployment on Hyper-V platforms.

All three pages say the password must not contain a $, &, >, <, ;, ' or ".

quotes: In the Zscaler Admin Console, create a dedicated username and password for the Branch Connector deployment.
The password must be at least 8 characters in length and include at least one uppercase letter, one number, and one special character.
The password must not contain a $ , &, >, <, ;, ', or ".
If the password does not meet these requirements, the deployment fails.
Create a dedicated password for the Branch Connector deployment in the Zscaler Admin Console.

esxi-version.statement: On VMware the VM requires VMware vSphere Hypervisor (ESXi) version 7.0 or later, or the minimum version stated by Broadcom.

quotes: The VM requires VMware vSphere Hypervisor (ESXi) version 7.0 or later, or the minimum version stated by Broadcom.

sizing-branch-connector.statement: On the VMware, Linux KVM and Hyper-V pages a Branch Connector VM requires, for Small, 4 GB of memory, 2 CPU cores, a 128 GB data disk and 2 NICs, and for Medium 8 GB of memory, 4 CPU cores, a 128 GB data disk and 4 NICs; the Hyper-V procedure enters 4096 for a Small VM or 8192 for a Medium VM, 2 or 4 virtual processors, and a total of two network adapters for Small or 4 for Medium.

quotes: Small VM: requires 4 GB of memory, 2 CPU cores, 128 GB data disk size, and 2 network interface cards (NICs)
Medium VM: requires 8 GB of memory, 4 CPU cores, 128 GB data disk size, and 4 NICs
Small VM: requires 4 GB of memory, two CPU cores, 128 GB data disk size, and 2 network interface cards (NIC)
Medium VM: requires 8 GB of memory, 4 CPU cores, 128 GB data disk size, and 4 NICs
Small VM: Requires 4 GB of memory, 2 CPU cores, 128 GB data disk size, and 2 network interface cards (NICs).
Medium VM: Requires 8 GB of memory, 4 CPU cores, 128 GB data disk size, and 4 NICs.
enter 4096 for a Small VM or 8192 for a Medium VM
In the Number of virtual processors field, select 2 for a Small VM or 4 for a Medium VM.
for a total of two network adapters for a Small VM or 4 network adapters for a Medium VM

sizing-combined-vmware.statement: On the VMware Branch Connector & App Connector page a combined VM requires, for Small, 16 GB of memory, 4 CPU cores, a 128 GB data disk and 3 NICs, and for Medium 32 GB of memory, 6 CPU cores, a 128 GB data disk and 5 NICs.

quotes: Small VM: requires 16 GB of memory, 4 CPU cores, 128 GB data disk size, and 3 network interface cards (NICs)
Medium VM: requires 32 GB of memory, 6 CPU cores, 128 GB data disk size, and 5 NICs

esxi-ha-vswitch.statement: For Branch Connector deployed in high availability on VMware, the Promiscuous mode option must be enabled (set to Accept) on the vSwitch or at the port group level, and the MAC address changes and Forged transmits options must be enabled on the vSwitch or port group. Branch Connector uses the Common Address Redundancy Protocol (CARP) to process traffic across multiple Branch Connector instances; when promiscuous mode is enabled other VMs might be able to detect traffic going through the service interface, and Zscaler recommends a port group for the Branch Connector service interfaces. If multiple physical ports exist on the same vSwitch, the Net.ReversePathFwdCheckPromisc advanced option must be enabled (set to 1) on the ESXi host, or multicast traffic loops back to the host and CARP does not function properly.

quotes: Review the virtual machine specifications for Branch Connector deployed in high availability.
The Promiscuous mode option must be enabled (i.e., set to Accept) on the vSphere switch (vSwitch) or at the port group level.
Branch Connector uses the Common Address Redundancy Protocol (CARP) to process traffic across multiple Branch Connector instances.
The MAC address changes option must be enabled on the vSwitch or port group.
The Forged transmits option must be enabled on the vSwitch or port group.
When promiscuous mode is enabled, other VMs might be able to detect traffic going through the service interface.
To avoid this risk, Zscaler recommends that you create and use a port group for your Branch Connector service interfaces.
If multiple physical ports exist on the same vSwitch, then the Net.ReversePathFwdCheckPromisc advanced option must be enabled (i.e., set to 1) on the ESXi host.
If it is not enabled, then multicast traffic loops back to the host, causing CARP not to function properly, and link states coalesced messages are sent.

hyperv-specifics.statement: On Hyper-V, MAC Address Spoofing must be enabled on each network adapter for Branch Connector deployed in high availability, and Zscaler recommends enabling it for non-HA deployments as well; the procedure selects Generation 1 as the VM generation to support the VHDX file, deselects Use Dynamic Memory for this virtual machine, and moves IDE above CD in the boot device Startup order list.

quotes: VM specification for Branch Connector deployed in high availability (HA): MAC Address Spoofing must be enabled on each network adapter.
MAC address spoofing must be enabled for high availability (HA) deployments. Zscaler recommends that you enable MAC address spoofing for non-HA deployments, as well.
select Generation 1 as the VM generation to support your VHDX file
Deselect the Use Dynamic Memory for this virtual machine checkbox.
In the boot device Startup order list, move IDE above CD.

kvm-specifics.statement: On Linux KVM the procedure selects Import existing disk image in the New VM window, selects Free BSD 11.4 as the operating system, and selects CDROM device as the Device type.

quotes: In the New VM window, select Import existing disk image.
For Choose the operating system you are installing, select Free BSD 11.4.
For Device type, select CDROM device from the drop-down menu, then click Finish.

user-data-required.statement: On VMware, deployments using cloud-init Config Drive require a text file of user data for the Branch Connector VM, applied to the VM as an ISO file mounted via a virtual CD-ROM drive during deployment, and deployments using an OVA file and OVA template instead have the OVA import process provide the user data; the file is named userdata.cfg and formatted in YAML. The Linux KVM and Hyper-V pages also require a text file containing user data information for the Branch Connector VM.

quotes: For deployments using cloud-init Config Drive, you must create a text file containing user data information for your Branch Connector VM.
This information is applied to the VM as an International Organization for Standardization (ISO) file that you mount via a virtual CD-ROM drive during deployment.
This section does not pertain to deployments using an OVA file and OVA template. In these deployments, the OVA file import process provides the user data information.
Create your user data in a text file named userdata.cfg using one of the following templates, formatted in YAML:
You must create a text file containing user data information for your Branch Connector VM.
You must create a text file containing user data information for your Branch Connector VM.

user-data-template.statement: The VMware page's Branch Connector with Management DHCP Template has a ZSCALER block with cc_url and http_probe_port, where a comment says the optional http_probe_port changes the port for load balancer status checks from the default value 50001 to 50035; the template also carries api_key, password, username and a network config with physical interface subnets of type dhcp, and a static variant gives an address, gateway and nameserver addresses.

quotes: ZSCALER: cc_url: <CC_URL> http_probe_port: 50035
#Optional to change the port for load balancer status checks from the default value 50001 to 50035.
evidence.after: Branch Connector with Management DHCP Template

quotes: api_key: <API Key> password: <Admin Password> username: <Admin Username> network: config: - name: <Driver> type: physical subnets: - type: dhcp version: '1' #ssh keys are optional
subnets: - address: <IP Address/Netmask> gateway: <Gateway> type: static - type: nameserver address: - <IP Address> - <IP Address> search: - zscaler.net

user-data-iso.statement: The VMware page applies the user data to the VM as an ISO image with one of three procedures, Windows, macOS or Linux, and in each the user data file must be named user-data. The Windows procedure uses oscdimg.exe with the volume label cidata (-lcidata), the macOS procedure uses mkisofs with -volid cidata, and the Linux procedure runs the geniosimage command with -volid cidata.

quotes: Apply your user data to the VM as an ISO image using one of the following procedures:
The user data file must be named user-data.
oscdimg.exe -j1 -u1 -lcidata .\isodir\user-data
evidence.after: Install the Development Tools component from the Windows ADK.

quotes: The user data file must be named user-data.
mkisofs -output user-data.iso -volid cidata -joliet -rock isodir/user-data
evidence.after: Install cdrtools using a method such as Homebrew. (This procedure uses Homebrew.)

quotes: The user data file must be named user-data.
geniosimage -o user-data.iso -volid cidata -joliet -rational-rock isodir/user-data

network-drivers.statement: The VMware page's user data names the interface driver for the chosen virtual NIC: vtnet for Windows VirtIO, em for Intel e1000, igb for Intel Gigabit, ix for Intel 10 Gigabit, vmx for VMware Vxnet3 and hn for Hyper-V.

quotes: Windows VirtIO: vtnet
Intel e1000: em
Intel Gigabit: igb
Intel 10 Gigabit: ix
VMware Vxnet3: vmx
Hyper-V: hn

ova-properties.statement: A VMware OVA deployment takes the Branch Connector Provisioning URL as the Provisioning Template URL, the API Key from the API Key Management page, a Management Interface Type of static or DHCP (the IP address and subnet prefix are entered if static and left blank if DHCP) and an SSH public key for logging in without a password; for Branch Connector & App Connector, an App Connector Provisioning Key is configured in the Admin Console, the Management Interface Type is static, a Provision Key is entered, and the Control Interface Type is static with the IP address and subnet prefix of the control interface.

quotes: Provisioning Template URL: Enter the Branch Connector Provisioning URL.
API Key: Enter the API Key from the API Key Management page.
Management Interface Type: Select static or DHCP.
Management Interface IP Address: If you selected static, enter the IP address and subnet prefix for the management interface. If you selected DHCP, leave blank.
ssh login public key: Enter the SSH public key for logging in without a password.
Configure an App Connector Provisioning Key in the Zscaler Admin Console.
Management Interface Type: Select static.
Provision Key: Enter the App Connector Provisioning Key.
Control Interface Type: Select static.
Control Interface IP Address: Enter the IP address and subnet prefix for the control interface.

combined-user-data.statement: The VMware Branch Connector & App Connector page gives a Branch Connector & App Connector with Static Management IP Template, which has an IP configuration for the App Connector interface and a zscaler_app_connector block with enable 'yes' and the provisioning key.

quotes: Branch Connector & App Connector with Static Management IP Template
#IP configuration for the App Connector interface
zscaler_app_connector: enable: 'yes' provisioning_key: <Key>

combined-vm-sizing.impact: The same combined image has four sets of CPU and NIC counts, and the KVM page also differs on memory; the pages do not say which governs, so a VM sized from one page may not match another.

permission-names.title: Whether provisioning and configuration permissions are one permission
permission-names.detail: The VMware and KVM pages name Branch Connector Provisioning permissions and the Hyper-V page names Branch Connector configuration permissions; no page says whether these are the same permission.
permission-names.blocks: Granting a deploying admin the right role.

host-versions.title: Minimum Linux KVM and Hyper-V host versions
host-versions.detail: Only the VMware page states a hypervisor version (ESXi 7.0 or later); the KVM and Hyper-V pages state none, and the KVM page does not name an image format.

combined-kvm-hyperv.title: App Connector provisioning on KVM and Hyper-V combined deployments
combined-kvm-hyperv.detail: The KVM and Hyper-V combined-image pages show the plain Branch Connector user-data templates, with no zscaler_app_connector block and no App Connector provisioning key prerequisite, unlike the VMware combined page; this is an absence found by comparing pages. How the App Connector is provisioned on those hypervisors is not stated.
combined-kvm-hyperv.blocks: Deploying a combined Branch Connector & App Connector on KVM or Hyper-V.

probe-port-range.title: Allowed range of http_probe_port
probe-port-range.detail: The user data template shows http_probe_port: 50035 and a comment naming the default 50001, but the allowed range is not stated.
probe-port-range.blocks: Choosing a load balancer status-check port.
